proposals.name: Memory and storage fade vs SMH
proposals.reason: Memory beat SMH by 5.7 points on 11-11 on CoreWeave's capex, a read-across, while the pair is in a 20% 60-session downtrend; the last four such jumps (6-25, 7-21, 7-30, 10-28) gave back 7.6-12.3 points inside five sessions, and spot DRAM and NAND are still slipping.

reasoning.what_changed: Equal-weight MU, SNDK, WDC, STX, SIMO rose 10.5% on 11-11 against SMH +4.8%, a 5.7-point lead (+2.1 sd), after lagging SMH by 8 points over 20 sessions; none of the five is above its 50-day.
reasoning.story: The jump was CoreWeave's 11-10 results (backlog $132.5B, 2026 capex floor $37-39B), not memory pricing news. Memory's own data is softer: DDR4 spot flat to down since 11-3, 512Gb TLC NAND wafers -4.3% in the week of 11-2, TrendForce's Q4 PC DRAM contract rise (+13-18%) slower than Q3's, Kioxia saying NAND prices are leveling off, and 2028-29 oversupply worries (CXMT, Counterpoint) behind the month-long lag.
reasoning.chart: The pair is down 20% in 60 sessions and below where it started every week since early October. In the past year, of nine days the basket beat SMH by more than 1.75 sd, the four inside the downtrend since June all reversed by 7.6-12.3 points within five sessions; the earlier five, in an uptrend, mostly ran on. The challenger found the same for 9-04, 9-18 and 10-28 at a 4-point threshold.
reasoning.coming: Applied Materials reports 11-12 after the close (in August a strong DRAM-capex message fed the oversupply worry; a weak one hits chips generally). Nvidia's board met late 11-11 on Huang's future; Nvidia reports 11-17 after the close, after this trade's last close. SanDisk's split is 11-19, outside the window.
reasoning.case_against: Demand data is strong (Korea chip exports +331% in 11-1 to 11-10; BofA sees the upcycle through 2027; Morgan Stanley prefers memory after the pullback), so the lead can hold. The basket moves about 1.5 times SMH, so equal dollars is a net short on chips: a relief rally, say if Nvidia's board keeps Huang, hurts. About 8% of SMH is MU and SK hynix, which mutes the hedge slightly, and 19% is Nvidia, whose CEO news is binary; the book already holds an NVDA short against QQQ. The evidence is four to seven days, partly overlapping the 11-05 crash. It didn't win because the 11-11 move is a read-across with no memory-price news behind it, inside a falling trend where every recent jump faded.

proposals.wrong_if: Memory beats SMH again on 11-13, the session after Applied's report, or TrendForce or DRAMeXchange show DRAM and NAND spot prices turning up inside the window.
proposals.hedge_why: SMH is the chip index memory trades against (basket correlation 0.87 over 60 sessions); the thesis is memory giving back its lead over chips, not a call on chips. Beta 1.44 leaves a net short on chips at equal dollars, said in case_against.

Filled overnight in full; about +0.7 points against the fills. Chips are down on the Nvidia CEO reports with no board decision announced; no memory-price news (TrendForce's 11-11 spot table: DDR4 -0.2%, DDR5 +0.1%). wrong_if is tested on 11-13 after Applied Materials reports tonight.
